cases.purpose: Run chgrp in the actual side shell with a controlled database; check distinct named and numeric GIDs and unknown-name failure without requiring diagnostic byte identity.
cases.oracle: GNU chgrp in reference shell with the same database and initial file ownership
cases.comparison: Status, diagnostic presence, and resulting gid for each call; tree snapshot.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mount --bind group.fixture /etc/group || { echo SETUP-FAILED; exit 99; }
/usr/bin/touch named numeric unknown
/usr/bin/chown 2000:2000 named numeric unknown || exit 99
run() {
  local label=$1 group=$2 file=$3 status
  chgrp "$group" "$file" > /tmp/chgrp.out 2> /tmp/chgrp.err
  status=$?
  printf '%s status=%s diagnostic=' "$label" "$status"
  if [[ -s /tmp/chgrp.err ]]; then printf yes; else printf no; fi
  printf ' gid='
  /usr/bin/stat -c '%g' "$file"
}
run named fixturestaff named
run numeric 3050 numeric
run unknown fixture-no-such-group unknown
cases.stdout:
named status=0 diagnostic=no gid=3050
numeric status=0 diagnostic=no gid=3050
unknown status=1 diagnostic=yes gid=2000
